clue.text: 25/12's first offering interest on top

indicators.note: on says the first piece sits on top of (before) the second

parts.note: an interest in a business is a share or part of it
a ridge is the top or crest of a hill or roof

explanation.surface: Someone paying interest up front, as if a bank charged a premium.
explanation.walkthrough: 25/12 is Christmas Day, written as a date; in the carol 'The Twelve Days of Christmas' the first gift is a bird in a pear tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In the carol, the true love's gift on the first day of Christmas is this bird in a pear tree.

clue.text: Settled shelters remain, though

indicators.note: shelters means the word for settled wraps round the word for remain

parts.note: alit means landed or settled, as a bird on a branch
to be is to exist or remain

explanation.surface: Settled shelters still stand, even so.
explanation.definitionFit: This conjunction means even if or although, a formal synonym for though.

clue.text: In conclusion, cracking shot

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the conclusion splits the attempt

parts.note: a shot at something is a try or attempt
a conclusion is an end

explanation.surface: A summing-up: in conclusion, that was a cracking shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In conclusion' looks like a set phrase; 'In' alone is the definition, meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in is in fashion, fashionable or stylish at the moment.

clue.text: One of the trainee doctors you may see, it's rumoured, sequentially

indicators.note: it's rumoured says the word is reported by ear, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.words: One of the trainee doctors you may see
parts.note: an intern is a junior doctor in training in a hospital

explanation.surface: A patient waiting to see each junior doctor on the ward, one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things one after another, each in its proper order, is doing them sequentially.

clue.text: In light of our West becoming Wilder, start to leave time for shooting

indicators.note: In says the starting letter goes inside the jumble
becoming wilder means the letters of light of our West run riot
start to means the first letter of leave

explanation.surface: A film-buff remark about Hollywood Westerns turning into Billy Wilder films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts L inside the anagram of LIGHT OF OUR WEST from 'becoming Wilder'. 12 August opens the British grouse-shooting season.
explanation.definitionFit: 12 August is the traditional British opening day of the red grouse shooting season.

clue.text: Excellent manufacturer of honey and fine meaty rations

parts.note: bully is a dated exclamation meaning excellent, as in 'bully for you'
a bee makes honey
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: Praise for a honey maker and its fine products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meaty rations' is the definition: tinned corned beef issued to soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: This tinned corned beef was the staple meat issue in British army rations.

clue.text: Heath-dwellers take advantage going round resort of ours

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

indicators.note: going round means the edge wraps round the other letters

parts.note: an edge is an advantage over rivals

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means the letters of ours are sorted again

explanation.surface: Locals cashing in on a nearby seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place; read as re-sort it is the anagram signal, giving ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: These game birds live on the heather moorland of Britain, so they are heath-dwellers.

clue.text: See 25
DJ sacked due to decking that's wrong

indicators.note: decking means covering or adorning, so the jumbled letters wrap round the mark
sacked means the words due to are ransacked, their letters jumbled

parts.note: a cross, X, is the mark a teacher puts by something wrong

explanation.surface: A disc jockey fired for some unspecified wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decking' puts X inside TUEDO, the anagram of DUE TO from 'sacked'. DJ is not a disc jockey but a dinner jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: DJ abbreviates dinner jacket, the formal evening jacket Americans call by this name.

clue.text: But indisposed to job in City parts?

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the City code goes into the middle of the jumble
indisposed means out of order, so the letters of to job in are rearranged

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to take a job in parts of the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' puts EC inside OBJTION, the anagram of TO JOB IN from 'indisposed'. A 'but' as a noun is a demurral, as in 'no ifs or buts'.
explanation.definitionFit: A but, used as a noun, is a demurral or protest raised against something.

clue.text: Help into narrow lead in match

definitions.meaning: a boost with cupped hands given to someone climbing into a saddle
in darts a match is played in legs, so being one leg ahead is a slim lead

explanation.surface: Assisting someone into a narrow lead in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a boost into the saddle, and also being one leg ahead in a darts match.

clue.text: Genius? No time to come to our country without it!

indicators.note: to come to says the next piece follows on from the first

parts.note: bird is slang for time in prison, from rhyming slang bird-lime

indicators.note: without means the word it is taken out of the country

parts.note: for a British setter, our country is Britain
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A boast that only a genius could reach Britain without some vital thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genius? No' is the definition: the opposite of a genius. 'Bird' is British slang for a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A dim, featherbrained person is the opposite of a genius, so a scornful 'genius? no' fits.

clue.text: East Indian residents grab Roman guards

indicators.note: guards means the words grab Roman keep the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Locals in the East Indies seizing Roman sentries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'residents' sounds like people; here they are plants native to the region.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a genus of shrubs native to tropical Asia, so its plants are residents of the East Indies.

clue.text: Mountain-dwellers harass scamp having grass cut up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to nag is to harass with complaints

indicators.note: having means the scamp holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, a scamp
to rat is to inform, as a grass does

explanation.surface: Hill folk harassing a rascal over some cut grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' turns the whole string NAGIMRATP upside down. 'grass' looks like a lawn but is British slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: This grouse lives on high, rocky mountain slopes, turning white in winter.

clue.text: A problem for corporation, beautiful woman appropriating pleasure craft endlessly

indicators.note: appropriating means taking in, so the woman holds the boat

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the boat is cut off

parts.note: a yacht is a pleasure craft

explanation.surface: A business headache caused by a beauty helping herself to a company yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is a jokey word for a paunch, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is old slang for a pot belly, so a stomach pain is a problem for it.

clue.text: It is cooking with dash of coriander in new rice pan

indicators.note: in says the cooked letters go inside the other jumble
new means the letters of rice take a new order
cooking means the letters of it is are stirred about
dash of means just the first letter of coriander

explanation.surface: A recipe step: stir a little coriander into rice in a fresh pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' looks like the cooking vessel; it is a verb, to slate.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan a play or film is to slate it, a synonym for finding fault harshly.

clue.text: Expression of one dissatisfied Egyptian King!

definitions.meaning: a click of disapproval made by someone displeased
the familiar short name for Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh

explanation.surface: An Egyptian pharaoh grumbling about something.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the clicking sound of disapproval, and the popular nickname of the pharaoh Tutankhamun.

clue.text: After Tango, both of us texting bird

indicators.note: After says the texting piece follows the T

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
in text speak you and I is written U I

explanation.surface: Two people texting each other after a tango.
explanation.definitionFit: The tui is a New Zealand honeyeater known for its white throat tuft.

clue.text: Not all the side plates may be put out for it

definitions.text: plates may be put out for it

indicators.note: not all means the last letter of the side is left off

parts.note: a sporting side is a team

explanation.surface: Not every player on the side gets a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: For an afternoon meal of sandwiches and cakes, plates are laid out.

clue.text: Now centre of 27 12 is a legitimate target

definitions.text: Now centre of 27 12 is a legitimate target

parts.words: Now centre of 27 12 is a legitimate target
parts.note: the middle letters of the answers to 27 and 12 run together spell GAMEBIRD; the clue describes the time from 12 August when such birds may lawfully be shot

explanation.surface: A cross-reference saying that something in the middle of two other answers may now be shot at.
explanation.walkthrough: From AFTERGAME and BIRDBRAIN take the centre, GAME BIRD. 12 August, the Glorious Twelfth, opens the shooting of red grouse in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The shooting period for red grouse opens on 12 August, when these birds become lawful quarry.

clue.text: I'm obliged to get behind independent oil producer

indicators.note: to get behind says the thanks piece comes after the independent piece

parts.note: ta is an informal British way of saying thanks

explanation.surface: Someone thanking you for backing an independent oil company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil producer' suggests a petroleum firm; it is a palm whose fruit yields oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The ita palm (moriche palm) of South America yields an oil from its fruit.

clue.text: Only Connect on after the watershed?

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in letter headings
in British TV the watershed is 9pm, after which adult content may be shown, so late at night

explanation.surface: Scheduling the TV quiz Only Connect after 9pm.
explanation.walkthrough: Only Connect is a BBC quiz show; the watershed is the 9pm cutoff on British TV before which unsuitable content is banned.
explanation.definitionFit: To link two ideas or establish a link between things is a synonym for to connect.

clue.text: Jersey etc having the last word over pictures

parts.note: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, CI

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the word is turned upside down

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer

explanation.surface: Jersey always getting the last word on the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the pictures' is British for a film theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures is an old British phrase for going to see films.

clue.text: Spot a Greek letter T inscribed

indicators.note: inscribed means written inside, so the T goes within

parts.note: sigma is the Greek letter s

explanation.surface: Noticing a T carved alongside a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot or mark on a plant or the skin, as in botany or medicine, is a synonym.

clue.text: Incite tomboy to enter gym

indicators.note: to enter means the tomboy goes inside the gym

parts.note: PT, physical training, is the school gym lesson
romp is an old word for a tomboy

explanation.surface: Urging a tomboy into the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur or move someone to act is a synonym for incite.

clue.text: Say (as client, e.g.): "I'm disgruntled with parrot"

definitions.text: Say (as client, e.g.): "I'm disgruntled with parrot"

indicators.note: disgruntled suggests the letters are put out of humour and out of order

parts.note: the two letters of I'm used as written

explanation.surface: A customer saying they are unhappy with the parrot they bought, Monty Python style.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of AS CLIENT EG, IM and PARROT gives the answer, and the whole clue is an example of doing it: the Dead Parrot sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer voicing displeasure about a purchase is lodging a formal grievance.

clue.text: Reversible section of fifth cranial graft

indicators.note: Reversible says the hidden letters are read backwards
section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A medical phrase about a nerve graft in the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: To inarch is to graft a plant by joining a shoot still attached to its own root to another stock.

clue.text: Taking advantage of 19 rematch

definitions.meaning: 19 is the start of shooting; to go out pursuing the quarry then, read as two words
a game played after the first, a return fixture

explanation.surface: A replay arranged to exploit the start of the shooting season.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one word, it is a subsequent game; read as two, it means pursuing quarry once the shooting opens.

clue.text: Horrified, heading off #crashed

indicators.note: crashed means smashed up, so the remaining letters are jumbled
heading off says the first letter of the symbol's name is dropped

parts.note: the symbol # is called a hashtag on social media

explanation.surface: A horrified social-media post tagged with the word crashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' takes H from HASHTAG, leaving ASHTAG, which 'crashed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone horrified is struck with shock and dismay, which is the meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: Rubbish about man with a tip for Simon Nye?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the slang word surrounds the rest

parts.note: pants is British slang for rubbish or nonsense
he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: tip for means the first letter of Simon

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at the sitcom writer Simon Nye's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon Nye wrote Men Behaving Badly, but only his surname is the definition: a nye (or nide) is a brood of a particular game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A nye is the collective noun for a brood of these long-tailed game birds.
